headline: United Airlines moves to restrict AI agents from booking flights
body: United Airlines says it will restrict access to AI agents that book flights and manage reservations for users, citing cybersecurity risk. The airline warns that “sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information”. TechCrunch reports that Bank of America last week urged customers not to share passwords with AI assistants.
note: Banks face the same problem of telling a customer from an AI system acting for one. United's answer is to restrict access.

evidence.text: United Airlines said it will restrict access to AI agents seeking to book flights and manage reservations on their users’ behalf, citing a risk to cybersecurity and undermining federal regulations.

United warns that “sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles.”
The move comes as airlines and banks are struggling to differentiate between real customers and AI systems operating on their behalf, such as when users share their logins with their AI assistants.
The airline’s move follows a warning from banks, including Bank of America, which last week urged customers not to share their passwords with their AI assistants.
